# More sophisticated piecewise revealing

## `#one-by-one`

`#pause` may be considered syntactically a bit cumbersome as it employs a
`show`-rule.
If you prefer to signal the grouping of content appearing together by using
a single function call, you can use `#one-by-one`:

```typ
#one-by-one[Do you know ][$pi$ ][to a thousand decimal places?]
```

resulting in

::: {layout-ncol=3}
![one-by-one (subslide 1)](one-by-one-1.png)

![one-by-one (subslide 2)](one-by-one-2.png)

![one-by-one (subslide 3)](one-by-one-3.png)
:::

If we still want to uncover certain elements one after the other but starting
on a later subslide, we can use the optional `start` argument of `#one-by-one`:

```typ
#one-by-one(start: 3)[This ][came ][pretty late.]
```

resulting in

::: {layout-ncol=3}
![one-by-one-start (subslide 1)](one-by-one-start-1.png)

![one-by-one-start (subslide 2)](one-by-one-start-2.png)

![one-by-one-start (subslide 3)](one-by-one-start-3.png)

![one-by-one-start (subslide 4)](one-by-one-start-4.png)

![one-by-one-start (subslide 5)](one-by-one-start-5.png)
:::

This optional `start` argument exists for all functions displayed on this page.

## `#item-by-item`

`#one-by-one` is especially useful for arbitrary contents that you want to display
in that manner.
Sometimes, it produces a bit too much syntactical noise with all the brackets
between content, though.
That is especially true for lists, enums, and term lists.
Instead of

```typ
#one-by-one[
  - first
][
  - second
][
  - third
]
```

you can also write

```typ
#item-by-item[
  - first
  - second
  - third
]
```

resulting in

::: {layout-ncol=3}
![item-by-item (subslide 1)](item-by-item-1.png)

![item-by-item (subslide 2)](item-by-item-2.png)

![item-by-item (subslide 3)](item-by-item-3.png)
:::

A more complex example involving enums and term lists:

```typ
#show: columns.with(3)

#set list(marker: sym.arrow)
#item-by-item[
  - first
  - second
    - some
    - detail
  - third
]
#colbreak()

#item-by-item[
  + also
  + works
  + with `enums`
]
#colbreak()

#item-by-item(start: 2)[
  / and: with
  / terms: too
]
```

::: {layout-ncol=3}
![item-by-item-complex (subslide 1)](item-by-item-complex-1.png)

![item-by-item-complex (subslide 2)](item-by-item-complex-2.png)

![item-by-item-complex (subslide 3)](item-by-item-complex-3.png)
:::

Note that the list markers and enum numbers are not hidden.
You can truly consider this a bug or a feature...

This is due to a [bug](https://github.com/typst/typst/issues/619) in typst.
See the
[FAQ](../faq/faq.qmd#is-it-possible-to-also-hide-the-markers-of-hidden-list-items)
for a workaround.
